_comment: Card data. Names, stats, foods and homes are drafts for owner and teacher review (all stats are deliberately exaggerated play numbers). Icons: src/data/card-icons.json. Locale keys: card.name.<id>, card.say.<id>, card.food.<id>, card.home.<id>, food.<food>, home.<home>, type.<type>.

animals.name: Sheru
animals.reviewNote: Carnivore: food shown as a plain covered bowl (food.meal), never a drumstick, prey or blood. Lions live in grassland and forest (Gir); 'jungle' is the child's word. Owner and teacher to approve.

animals.name: Veeru
animals.reviewNote: Carnivore: plain covered bowl, no prey or hunting. Owner and teacher to approve.

animals.name: Gajju
animals.reviewNote: Mostly grass, leaves, bark and fruit; sugarcane (a favourite) is the food shown on the card and in Forage Trail.

animals.name: Balu
animals.reviewNote: The emoji is a brown bear; the Indian sloth bear eats termites, fruit and honey. Honey kept as the icon.

animals.name: Neelu
animals.reviewNote: Peacocks also eat insects; seeds is a simplification.

animals.name: Gauri
animals.reviewNote: Farm shelf only (agreed rule). Sacred to many families: keep respectful, no jokes at the cow's expense.

animals.name: Chetak
animals.reviewNote: A horse as a farm animal is a simplification (also a working animal).

animals.name: Moti
animals.reviewNote: Many Indian dogs are street dogs; later content question. Bone is the common picture.

animals.name: Mini
animals.reviewNote: 'Cats drink milk' is a common child belief that adults may flag.

animals.name: Bittu
animals.reviewNote: Renamed from Chiku (the sparrow character); owner to approve the name.
